description:
We're Teleport, a team of curious builders passionate about space, science and technology. We enjoy solving real-world problems through software development, AI/ML, data analysis and creative thinking.

We're looking for enthusiastic collaborators with skills in Python, machine learning, data science, satellite imagery, Earth science and data visualisation. If you love experimenting, building and thinking beyond boundaries, come build something extraordinary with us!
summary:
Teleport is a satellite observation harmonisation platform designed to bring NASA's MODIS and VIIRS active-fire observations into a unified analytical view.

Although both sensors detect thermal anomalies, differences in their spatial resolution, observation times and measurement characteristics make direct comparison challenging. Teleport addresses this by using spatial and temporal analysis to identify potentially related observations, while preserving each sensor's original data and provenance.

The approach uses a common 1 km equal-area grid and candidate matching based on a distance threshold of 1 km and a time difference of up to 60 minutes. It retains unmatched observations and supports multiple possible associations rather than forcing detections into one-to-one matches. The platform is designed to support geographical exploration, historical fire-activity analysis and sensor comparison.

Teleport is important because reliable interpretation of satellite fire data requires more than plotting hotspots on a map. By making sensor differences, observation coverage and uncertainty explicit, it aims to help researchers, environmental teams and decision-makers explore thermal activity more responsibly.

Our guiding principle is simple: harmonise the observations, not the truth behind them.
details:
The Problem

MODIS and VIIRS provide valuable satellite-based active-fire observations, but their differences in spatial resolution and observation characteristics make direct comparison challenging. Understanding historical fire activity requires more than simply displaying hotspot locations on a map.

Our Approach

Teleport focuses on harmonising these observations while preserving their original sensor information.

Our proposed methodology uses spatial and temporal proximity to identify potentially related observations. It retains original records and distinguishes candidate associations from unmatched observations rather than assuming that nearby detections represent the same physical fire.

A common 1 km equal-area analysis grid provides a shared spatial framework for comparing sensor observations. The platform's analytical approach also considers historical activity, sensor-specific measurements and satellite observation coverage.

Technology

The planned technology stack includes Python, FastAPI, React, TypeScript, PostgreSQL and PostGIS, alongside geospatial and data-analysis libraries.

Impact

Teleport aims to make satellite-derived thermal activity easier to explore across geographical areas and historical periods. It is designed to support researchers, emergency responders and environmental decision-makers through more transparent sensor comparison and historical analysis.

Scientific Responsibility

A satellite hotspot is a thermal observation, not necessarily a confirmed wildfire. Teleport preserves this distinction and communicates uncertainty, missing coverage and the limitations of cross-sensor associations.
